title: Optimal multilinear-formula size of the permanent
formal: Determine the growth of \(\log _{2} F(n)\) up to universal multiplicative constants as \(n\to \infty\), where \(F(n)\) is the minimum size of a multilinear arithmetic formula over \(\mathbb{C}\) computing \(\operatorname{perm}_{n}\). Equivalently, find a positive function \(g(n)\) and constants \(a,A>0,n_{0}\) such that \(2^{a g(n)}\le F(n)\le 2^{A g(n)}\) for every integer \(n\ge n_{0}\).
definitions: The permanent is \(\operatorname{perm}_{n}(X)=\sum_{\pi \in S_{n}}\prod _{i=1}^{n} x_{i,\pi (i)}\). An arithmetic formula is a finite rooted tree with variable or complex-constant leaves and binary addition or multiplication gates, evaluated as a commutative polynomial. Every gate must compute a multilinear polynomial: every variable has degree at most one in every monomial after cancellation. The formula must agree identically with \(\operatorname{perm}_{n}\) on \(\mathbb{C} ^{n^{2}}\), not merely on Boolean inputs. Size counts all gates, including leaves. No restriction on the numerical complexity of complex constants is imposed. Let \(F(n)\) be the minimum such size; it is attained because sizes are positive integers and the defining sum of monomials is a valid finite multilinear formula. The independent variables are the \(n^{2}\) entries of the matrix; n denotes its row count. Internal computations are required to be multilinear as polynomials after cancellation, not just at the output. Sharing of subexpressions is forbidden by the tree model. The requested precision is constant factors in \(\log _{2} F(n)\), not constant factors in \(F(n)\).

context_blocks.text: Multilinear formulas give a restricted but important setting in which superpolynomial lower bounds are known for an explicit central polynomial. The exponential target asks how far that separation can be taken even after substantial algebraic structure is imposed.

Raz’s lower bound grows as \(n^{\Omega (\log  n)}\), which is superpolynomial but not exponential in n. The broader permanent circuit problem permits sharing subcomputations and intermediate nonmultilinear polynomials, so these are not interchangeable targets. The survey records the unresolved exponential strengthening.

context_blocks.title: The full exponent instead of one proposed endpoint
context_blocks.text: The original conjecture asks for \(F(n)\ge 2^{cn}\). The retained card asks for its actual growth on the logarithmic scale, allowing an intermediate answer. Raz’s lower bound is \(n^{\Omega (\log  n)}\); the standard inclusion-exclusion formula gives an upper bound \(2^{O(n)}\) and is multilinear at every gate because its factors use different rows. No equivalence between the new determination task and the original conjecture is asserted.

why: Establish a qualitatively stronger explicit algebraic lower bound in one of the few models already admitting superpolynomial separations.
answer_criterion: Give a positive function \(g(n)\) and prove the two bounds displayed in the statement for the specified formula model, with constants independent of n. Merely restating \(\log _{2} F(n)\), proving a bound for constant depth or prohibiting cancellation adds restrictions not present here. This is an asymptotic exponent target, not a pointwise 0.01 approximation. The original exponential lower-bound conjecture would give \(g(n)=n\), using the known exponential-size upper bound.

sentences: The permanent is a canonical polynomial whose algebraic complexity captures a major explicit lower-bound challenge.
A formula is a tree of additions and multiplications without shared intermediate results.
Every intermediate polynomial must be multilinear, with complex constants and cancellation permitted.
The question asks for the growth of the logarithm of the smallest formula size, up to constant factors.
The known quasipolynomial lower bound and exponential upper bound leave a qualitative gap, with an exponential lower bound as the original conjectured endpoint.
